gap_at_outboard_midplane.description: Gap at the outboard midplane is the signed major-radius separation between a measurement position and the magnetic separatrix after mapping the position along its magnetic flux surface to the outboard midplane. Positive values indicate a position outside the separatrix, in the scrape-off layer.
gap_at_outboard_midplane.documentation:
Gap at outboard midplane

The gap is defined by

$$
g = R_{\mathrm{pos,mid}} - R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}
$$

where $g$ is the gap at the outboard midplane, $R_{\mathrm{pos,mid}}$ is the major-radius coordinate of the mapped measurement position at the outboard midplane, and $R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the major-radius coordinate of the magnetic separatrix there. Both terms in the difference are outboard-midplane major radii of the type defined by the [radial coordinate at outboard midplane](name:radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane), expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies pointwise to one measurement position, its assigned magnetic flux surface, and one selected magnetic separatrix, with no flux-surface, spatial, species, or time aggregation. It is a signed major-radius projection at the outboard midplane, not a shortest Euclidean clearance such as the [gap at plasma boundary] or the [gap at closest wall point](name:gap_at_closest_wall_point), not a plasma-wall clearance, and not the separation between inner and outer separatrices.

Mapping along the magnetic flux surface converts the original position into a common outboard-midplane reference before the major-radius difference is taken, so positions located anywhere on a flux surface can be compared on the same separatrix-relative scale.

Sign convention: Positive when the mapped measurement position lies outside the magnetic separatrix, at larger major radius $R$ than the separatrix at the outboard midplane, and therefore in the scrape-off layer.

Low-field-side (outboard) equatorial midplane. The outer-midplane reference follows the DD midplane_identifier (default option 'dr_dz_zero_sep': the outboard separatrix point where dr/dz = 0). For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $Z = Z_{\mathrm{mid}},\quad R > R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $Z_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is the midplane height the data's midplane identifier selects, the magnetic-axis height when none is given; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_m.description: Radial distance from the plasma boundary at the outboard midplane, positive outside it.
